_comment: Deck-out: the passive opponent runs out of library and loses (CR 104.3c).
Before core/OpponentDeck.h existed the opponent had NO library at all, so milling or
decking them could not win and could not even be attempted -- see
Two cards left. They draw at the END of each of OUR turns, so: our T1 -> 2->1,
our T2 -> 1->0, our T3 -> empty -> decked. The expected win turn is 3, OUR turn,
per the user's rule (2026-09-02): a decked opponent never gets a main phase, so the
game is over as of our last turn rather than their next one.
The board is deliberately EMPTY of any clock -- no attacker, no burn -- so the only
thing that can produce a win here is the deck-out. Auras is a deck with no way to touch
the opponent's library, which makes the point twice: the opponent_library_size field is
what turns the path on, and every deck without it is unaffected.
